messages:
sasha: heads up — after last night's key-rotation rollout I'm seeing a noticeable hit-rate delta between hosted and private for the prompt-prefix cache. hosted ~81.7%, private ~63.9% on the same traffic slice. did the rotation touch any netstore/key-normalization codepaths? :eyes:

raj: saw the alert. grabbing traces now. initial hypothesis: key-version header is present in hosted path but missing in some private control-plane requests, so netstore keys don't match v2 namespace. also checking metadata sanitizer changes from the rollout.

infra-bot: deploy status: key-rotation/v2 rolled to all clusters (hosted + private control-plane) at 2025-02-12T03:22Z. no automated rollback triggered.

mila: quick note — private deployments often have the netstore mounted via NFS gateway with case-insensitive mountopts in a few customer configs. if we changed kebab -> camel key normalization in v2 that could cause mismatches. can we diff object keys on a sample tenant?

raj: good point. running a small diff. here's the telemetry query I'm using (runs against telemetry-snap):
```
SELECT key_version, netstore_path, count(*) as cnt, avg(hit) as hit_rate
FROM prefix_cache_events
WHERE sample_window = 'last_30m' AND model = 'redwood-1x'
GROUP BY key_version, netstore_path
ORDER BY key_version DESC, cnt DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

raj: sample output (trimmed):
```
v2 | s3://hosted-cache/| 124k | 0.817
v2 | nfs://tenant-xyz/|  41k | 0.639
v1 | s3://hosted-cache/| 98k  | 0.795
v1 | nfs://tenant-xyz/| 39k  | 0.652
```

oliver: interesting — v1 had smaller delta. v2 hit-rate dropped much more on NFS paths. that points to key canonicalization or a netstore write path issue during rotation. also check ACLs: if we wrote keys with a different ACL/metadata they might be invisible to read calls from private nodes.

mila: I checked a single object on a private netstore: keys exist but the object metadata shows header `x-redwood-kv-version: v2-rotated` on writes from the control-plane, whereas read path expects `x-redwood-kv-version: v2`. a small suffix mismatch would make read miss.

sasha: ugh. where could that suffix get added? the compaction/serialize layer? kernel-selection code shouldn't touch headers. maybe the rollout changed the key-generator to append a fingerprint for collision mitigation (simhash-based) but only the writer included it.

raj: reproducing locally by forcing the key-generator to include simhash suffix. compare: `prefix|model|v2` vs `prefix|model|v2|sh-0x1f2a`. read path strips suffix only if flag ENABLE_SIMHASH_STRIP=true. looks like private deployments don't have that flag enabled in some control-plane configs.

sasha: that explains asymmetric behavior. hosted control-plane enabled strip, private didn't so we wrote keys with suffix but read didn't know to strip. can we hotfix by making read path tolerant (normalize by removing `sh-` suffix) and rolling to private? low-risk string normalize.

oliver: agree. proposed plan: 1) quick fix to read normalization (accept both with/without sh- suffix), 2) backfill a small canary rewriter that reads objects with sh- suffix and writes canonical keys for private tenants, 3) add e2e test that covers key-version + suffix mismatch.

mila: note: for some private netstores we also saw higher put latency (~30-120ms extra) after rotation which could be a separate issue (gateway throttling). I'll open a follow-up if write latency correlates with failed reads.

raj: created a canary branch and a toggle: `CACHE_KEY_SIMHASH_STRIP=true`. i'll push a canary to three private clusters and sample hit-rate for 15m. will post numbers here.

sasha: thanks — also add a quick telemetry tag so we can slice by `key_normalization=v2-suffix-fix`. sample script for sampling: 
```
# curl telemetry api to get tenant-level hit delta
curl -s -X POST https://telemetry.internal/query -H 'Authorization: Bearer $T' -d '{"q":"prefix_cache.hit_rate(slice=15m,filter=tenant:\"tenant-xyz\")"}' | jq '.'
```

infra-bot: canary deployment queued: cache-key-normalize-canary -> private-us-east-1a (3 nodes). started 2025-02-12T04:10Z.

raj: canary results after 12m: hosted-vs-private delta reduced for tenant-xyz: hosted 82.1% -> private 79.8% (was 63.9%). sampling across 5 tenants shows average private hit increasing +12.6 p.p. after toggle.

mila: nice. looks like suffix-stripping is the main cause. still want to follow up on put latency and potential NFS metadata behavior (ACLs).

sasha: final action items: 
- raj: ship normalization PR (read-tolerant) + toggle off by default until we backfill.
- oliver: add e2e that covers simhash suffix and netstore mount permutations.
- mila: investigate write latency and netstore gateway throttling on private configs.
- infra-bot: label rollout as `investigation-fixed` when normalization PR merges.

sasha: thanks team. leaving this thread open until PR merged and backfill verified. :thumbsup:
